name: ITC
step12_scaling_decision: A five-year projection of the credit path WAS built (Companies/itc/forward_model.py), with base and stress cases, and THREE Step 12b scorecards were filled - one per rating agency, since ITC was rated by ICRA (09-Jul-2026), CareEdge and CRISIL (both 11-Jul-2026) out of this one case folder. What was NOT run is the equity-research plugin's native 3-statement workbook. Reason: ITC holds Rs 23,759.43 crore of liquid assets against Rs 2,399.06 crore of debt including leases - liquid assets are 9.9 times total debt - and generates Rs 18,464.31 crore of operating cash flow against Rs 2,182.89 crore of capex. There is no financing question for a three-statement model to answer. The one forward variable that matters is the February 2026 cigarette tax reset, which FY2026 reflects for only TWO MONTHS and FY2027 will reflect for twelve: GST moved from 28% of transaction value to 40% of retail sale price with a steep excise hike on the phasing out of Compensation Cess. Its effect is already visible in FY2026 - gross cigarette revenue rose 13.1% while revenue NET of excise was FLAT at -0.2%, so the entire gross growth was tax. The model is built on net operating income for that reason, and deliberately does NOT annualise the excise line: the annual report gives no month-wise split, so any such split would be invented, and the GST component does not pass through reported revenue at all. The stress case flexes legal cigarette VOLUME, which is the company's own stated risk. Twelve opening-balance tie-outs. Recorded 01-Sep-2026.
